title: BehaviorMem: Building and Evaluating User Memory from Real-World E-Commerce Behavior Streams
abstract: arXiv:2610.34790v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: User memory helps personalized systems build on their understanding of users over time. In e-commerce, users convey their preferences and needs through both explicit language and implicit interactions with products. We study memory built from logs of these interactions, examining how it can \emph{remember} concrete evidence and established interests, and use that evidence to \emph{infer} underlying needs and preferences that inform judgments beyond well-observed product domains. Existing memory methods primarily target language-based interactions, and evaluations offer limited real behavioral data and limited separation of these capabilities. This leaves open how to jointly support and separately evaluate remembering and inference from behavioral logs. We formulate the problem of continual behavioral user memory around these joint requirements and develop a dedicated evaluation framework and memory method to address them. \textbf{Behavio

translated_title: BehaviorMem：从真实世界电商行为流中构建与评估用户记忆
translated_abstract: 用户记忆能够帮助个性化系统随时间不断加深对用户的理解。在电子商务中，用户通过显式语言和与产品的隐式交互来表达他们的偏好和需求。我们研究从这些交互日志中构建的记忆，考察它如何“记住”具体的证据和已确立的兴趣，并利用这些证据来“推断”潜在的需求和偏好，从而为超出充分观察到的产品领域之外的判断提供依据。现有的记忆方法主要针对基于语言的交互，且相关评估提供的真实行为数据有限，对这些能力的区分也不充分。这使得如何从行为日志中同时支持并分别评估“记忆”与“推断”仍是一个开放问题。我们围绕这些联合需求形式化了持续性行为用户记忆问题，并开发了专门的评估框架和记忆方法来解决这些问题。
tldr: 该论文提出BehaviorMem，一个基于真实电商行为流构建用户记忆的方法与评估框架，能够同时支持并分别评估“记住具体证据与兴趣”和“推断潜在需求与偏好”这两种核心能力。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes BehaviorMem, a memory method and evaluation framework built from real-world e-commerce behavior streams that jointly supports and separately evaluates remembering concrete evidence and inferring underlying user needs and preferences.
